value.overview: The Brown-headed Nuthatch (Sitta pusilla) is a nuthatch recorded in the United States. Field recognition often comes from small nuthatch shape, brown cap, white cheeks, bluish back, and nasal calls in pine woods. In the U.S. source data, it appeared in 14 state or DC summaries, including AL, AR, DE, FL, GA, LA, MD, MS, NC, OK, SC, TN, TX, VA. It is most associated with Forests:  Temperate Eastern, and local season should be checked before trip planning.
value.classification: The Brown-headed Nuthatch belongs to the family Nuthatches in the order Passeriformes. This is the practical birding classification used for the BirdIntel profile cache.
value.identification: Look for small nuthatch shape, brown cap, white cheeks, bluish back, and nasal calls in pine woods. Also use size, posture, flight style, voice, behavior, habitat, and season. Plumage can vary by sex, age, molt, and light, so the safest identification comes from combining several field marks rather than relying on one color or feature.
